answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a mirror ledger: every trade is mirrored into a public receipt that peers re-verify, so a fake identity cannot invent a history — it must show a river of checkable transactions flowing through established counterparties. A new identity starts with an ivory-clean slate worth nothing until it accumulates attested work, and each attestation costs the attestor reputation if the work proves fake. Spinning up a thousand fakes means buying a thousand real transaction histories, each priced in time and fees, while honest agents keep the reputation they earned.
